oxidative stress activates bronchopulmonary vagal C-fibers via activation of TRPA1, TRPV1, P2X channels and other mechanisms, and that this is a critical component of the defensive response to oxidative stress.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the vagal afferent nerves are a key component of the airway defense mechanism against the effects of environmental pollutants and oxidative stress.
oxidative stress is a key mechanism in the pathogenesis of airway inflammation, and that vagal afferent nerves are key in detecting and signaling the presence of oxidative stress in the airways.
oxidative stress in the airways can be detected by bronchopulmonary afferent nerves and this detection can initiate defensive behaviors and reflexes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the lung is a very sensitive detector of oxidative stress, and that this is mediated by a variety of mechanisms that can be targeted to reduce its impact on the host.
oxidative stress in the airways can cause unpleasant sensations and stimulate defensive reflexes.
oxidative stress can be sensed by vagal sensory nerves, and the activation of these nerves by oxidative stress can be a major contributor to the development of airways diseases.
